title: Understanding the Equations
text: The equations represent the optimization problems for finding the coefficients in linear regression. The first equation is for the original data, and the second is for the mean-centered data.

title: Mean-Centering Effect
text: Mean-centering the data affects the intercept term but not the other coefficients. This is because centering the data shifts it to have a mean of zero, which changes the intercept but not the slope.

title: MSE Comparison
text: The mean squared error (MSE) measures the average squared difference between the observed actual outcomes and the outcomes predicted by the model. When data is mean-centered, the MSE remains the same because the centering does not affect the variance of the errors.
